title: The 5 Best Alternatives to Zluri (2026)
summary: Compare 5 Zluri alternatives for 2026: AccessOwl, Torii, Zylo, Lumos and Cledara. See which fit access vs spend management, provisioning and pricing.
body_markdown:
Zluri is often bought with the CFO in mind, and the IT team is tasked with running it. With SaaS and AI sprawl, the ROI of spend management is straightforward. The first run finds duplicate tools and unused licenses and gives you leverage to renegotiate contracts. The problem buyers face is that after that first year clean-up, you've unlocked most of the value, but you're still paying for the spend tool every year.


That's why many SaaS management tools now include spend management as a feature rather than the whole product. This guide compares five Zluri alternatives. It's based on our research and on conversations with 450+ IT buyers who evaluated an access management solution, including teams that assessed or used Zluri. For a one-on-one view, see our[Zluri vs AccessOwl comparison](https://www.accessowl.com/alternatives/zluri-vs-accessowl) .


## TL;DR


Zluri is good at what it focuses on. It began as a SaaS spend management platform, built around discovery, license counts and spend, and it's one of the most thorough tools on the market for finding apps. Access workflows were added on top in 2024, and provisioning still runs through each app's API. So the right alternative depends on which job you most care about.


-


AccessOwl is the best alternative if the job is SaaS access management. It automates onboarding, offboarding, access requests and reviews in 500+ apps with no SCIM needed, and it includes spend features too.


-


Torii is the closest like-for-like if the job is still SaaS spend and Finance is the buyer.


-


Zylo is best for large enterprises that want deeper spend control across many business units.


-


Lumos is best for large enterprises focused on access management, with Okta at the centre of their stack.


-


Cledara is a lesser-known pick for finance teams that own software spend.


## Zluri was acquired by Infotech


In October 2026, the IT research firm Infotech acquired Zluri. Zluri's discovery and identity governance products will become modules of Infotech's new CIO Analytics platform.


Acquisitions often bring changes to pricing, packaging and the roadmap. It's not yet clear where access management will fit inside an analytics platform built for CIOs. If you're looking at alternatives to Zluri after the news, AccessOwl is a good fit for SaaS access management. Access is our whole product, not a module. We automate onboarding, offboarding, access requests and reviews in 500+ apps, with no SCIM needed.


## Why teams look for a Zluri alternative


Zluri is very good at what it started with. It finds the apps a company uses through nine discovery methods, including a browser extension and a desktop agent, and shows who uses them and what they cost.


The gaps show up when access management becomes the main job. Buyers we talked to who assessed Zluri ran into three problems.


### Zluri provisioning depends on each app's API


Zluri's docs describe automatic provisioning for "Apps that support provisioning via API, SCIM, or native connectors." When an app has no integration, the step becomes a manual task for its owner. Many vendors also keep user management on their top plan, so automating an app can mean upgrading it for the whole company first. That's the[SSO tax](https://www.ssotax.org/) . Zluri added browser based automation in 2026, and its help center documents it for two apps so far. AccessOwl supports 500+.


An IT engineer at a managed service provider compared both tools for a client and told us:


> "I found that AccessOwl was ahead in terms of provisioning. Zluri only allows provisioning through API. So it depends on the API permissions you have, whether you have the enterprise subscription to all the tools that would require. Slack's a great example where AccessOwl gets around that, but Zluri doesn't."
>
>
> IT engineer at a managed service provider


### Zluri access management is one module in a broad suite


Zluri now sells four products: identity visibility, identity governance, identity security posture and SaaS management. That breadth is the pitch, but it can read as more depth than there is. Zluri's own comparison pages call the web portal "the primary request surface" and rate Zluri "Trailing" on time-bound access. Teams that mainly need access automation end up paying for a large platform where access is one part.


### Zluri is built and priced for enterprises


Zluri sells to "enterprise security and IT teams" and doesn't publish pricing. It says "customer-reported go-live is typically 4–12 weeks depending on scope."


## How we ranked these Zluri alternatives


We compared these tools on the questions that decide most of our buyer conversations, not on the length of a feature list:


-


Access management or spend management first: Was the tool built for access management, or for spend with access added later?


-


Account management, not just visibility: How many apps does it actually create and remove accounts in, out of the box?


-


SSO and SCIM tax: Does automating an app mean upgrading it to an enterprise plan first?


-


Rollout: How long until onboarding and offboarding run on their own, and who has to run the tool?


-


Pricing: Is it published, or gated behind a sales process?


## AccessOwl: The Best Zluri Alternative for SaaS Access Management


If you're looking for a solution to automate SaaS access and user review audits, AccessOwl is the strongest choice. Zluri started adding access features over the last couple of years, but their core product is still spend. Access management has always been AccessOwl's core focus. AccessOwl is for the IT team, or the person who takes care of IT on the side, who wants SaaS access to run on its own from an employee's first day to their last.


That matters most when someone leaves. In our[State of SaaS Access Management 2026](https://www.accessowl.com/blog/state-of-saas-access-management-2026) report, a leaver had to be removed from a median of 17 apps, held by 8 different app admins. Without automation, that's 8 people to chase every time someone leaves.


### AccessOwl features


-


Onboarding: Give new hires access to every app they need before day one, without going into each app's admin console. A start date in your HR system creates the accounts, with the right permissions, groups and workspaces.


-


Offboarding: Remove access to all apps when someone leaves, not just the ones behind single sign-on. Once the last workday passes, AccessOwl removes the accounts, frees the licenses and logs each step.


-


Self-serve access requests: Employees ask for the app they need. The approver signs off in one click, and AccessOwl creates the account automatically.


-


User access reviews: User lists are pulled from each app automatically. Access a reviewer flags is removed during the review, and the evidence is ready for SOC 2 and ISO 27001 auditors.


-


500+ apps with no SCIM needed: Most apps connect through an integration account, so there's no SCIM or API setup and no upgrade to an app's enterprise plan. Every one of the[496 SaaS apps in our catalog](https://www.accessowl.com/integrations) supports provisioning and deprovisioning.


On Slack, employees request access with /request and approvers sign off right there, through our[native Slack app](https://www.accessowl.com/slack) . Teams that don't use Slack do the same from the web dashboard.


> "Since we started using AccessOwl I haven't received a single direct message to request access to tools."
>
>
> Khalifah Alsadah, Product Manager, from[Sary's success story](https://www.accessowl.com/customers/sary)


Maxio's two-person IT team used to spend 45 minutes to an hour onboarding each new hire. Here's how their Sr. IT Manager describes it now:


> "Onboarding now takes five to ten minutes if you're not distracted, tops"
>
>
> Shane Fritts, Sr. IT Manager, from[Maxio's success story](https://www.accessowl.com/customers/maxio)


### Who AccessOwl is built for


AccessOwl fits companies of roughly 30 to 1,000 people. Zluri and Torii also sell to mid-market companies. AccessOwl is built to own the access problem, not to add access on top of a spend platform.


The person who runs access may vary. Some companies have a solo IT admin or a small IT team. A common profile we see is a senior HR or Ops person who wants onboarding and offboarding to run more smoothly. They're often the one creating accounts by hand from a checklist, chasing app admins for access and hoping nothing gets missed when someone leaves. AccessOwl lets that person set up the workflows once and let them run.


AccessOwl doesn't offer SSO or MFA, so you keep Google Workspace, Microsoft or your identity provider for sign-in.


### Why AccessOwl is the best fit for mid-market companies


**Pricing you can see.**[AccessOwl's pricing is public](https://www.accessowl.com/pricing) . It starts at $250 a month, and there's a 7-day free trial. You don't have to book a demo to find out what it costs.


**Spend management as a feature.** AccessOwl covers the spend side too, without making it the whole product. It finds shadow apps through Google and Microsoft sign-ins, tracks what each app costs and reminds app owners before renewals. Licenses are freed when someone leaves instead of sitting on a suspended account.


**Built for Google Workspace and Microsoft 365.** AccessOwl layers on top of[Google Workspace](https://www.accessowl.com/google-workspace) or[Microsoft 365](https://www.accessowl.com/microsoft-365) . Connecting takes minutes, and there's no migration or heavy setup. It works with your identity provider, including Okta, and with 50+ HR systems, so joiners and leavers start from the data you already have.


**API, MCP and AI skills.** AccessOwl has an API and MCP, plus premade[AccessOwl skills](https://docs.accessowl.com/guides/ai/accessowl-skills) for AI assistants like Claude and Codex. Your IT team can ask its AI tool to onboard a new hire, check what someone has access to, mirror a teammate's access or schedule an offboarding. The AI never approves anything. Every request it creates follows your normal approval policies.


### Bottom line


If you're replacing Zluri because access is the real job, AccessOwl gets onboarding, offboarding, requests and access reviews running across 500+ apps without SCIM or enterprise plan upgrades. It sits on top of Google Workspace or Microsoft 365, covers spend as a feature and publishes its pricing, so a mid-market team can be live in days.

## Torii (best when SaaS spend is still the job)


Torii is the closest match to Zluri. Both began as SaaS spend management platforms, and Torii is a great product for what it was built for. It finds the apps you use, shows you what you spend and helps you cut what you don't need. If Finance is buying a way to see and cut SaaS spend, Torii belongs on your list.


The risk is buying it for access management, because it runs into many of the same limits as Zluri. An information security manager at a 150-person hospitality software company trialled both Torii and AccessOwl. What decided it for them was how accounts get created:


> "For me, the most important feature is the fact that AccessOwl's provisioning does not rely on SCIM. And I really love the fact that you can rely on an integration account for some more provisioning, deprovisioning."
>
>
> Information security manager, 150-person hospitality software company


### What Torii offers


-


Shadow IT discovery from a browser extension, SSO and identity provider data, and finance and expense tools.


-


License and spend tracking, renewals and contract management.


-


An App Access Catalog, generally available since July 2026, with access profiles, approval flows and time-limited access.


-


Access requests from the web catalog, Slack or Microsoft Teams, its API or MCP.


-


No-code onboarding and offboarding workflows, triggered from your HR system.


-


Access reviews on its Enterprise plan.


### Where it falls short


Provisioning depends on each app's API. Torii's integration directory lists 298 apps. Only 105 of them list actions to both create and remove a user, and 168 list no actions at all, so they give you visibility but can't change who has access. For apps outside the list you can build your own connection, but the app still needs a user-management API. Torii's own Slack docs say "Managing users from within Torii requires a Business+ or Enterprise Grid account."


Access workflows often end in a manual task. Torii's App Access Catalog, generally available since July 2026, added approval flows and time-limited access. But by default, an approved request emails the app owner. When temporary access expires, Torii's docs say "Every organization starts with a default deprovisioning workflow that creates a Revoke access task for the app owner." Access is only granted or removed automatically when you build an API workflow for that app.


Access reviews are newer. Torii added them in 2025 on its Enterprise plan, and automated remediation arrived in August 2026.


Torii doesn't publish pricing.[Vendr's data](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/torii) puts the median buyer at about $32,000 a year. We break down the differences in our[Torii comparison](https://www.accessowl.com/alternatives/torii-vs-accessowl) .


### Where it fits


Torii fits companies where Finance is the buyer and the main goal is to see and cut SaaS spend. Its shadow IT detection, dashboards and contract handling are genuinely strong. It also suits teams that have IT time to build API workflows for each app they want automated.


## Zylo (best for large enterprises focused on SaaS spend)


Zylo is one of the original SaaS management platforms, and buyers we talk to often shortlist it next to Zluri. It calls itself "the leading enterprise SaaS spend management platform" and is built for IT, procurement and FinOps teams at very large companies. Discovery starts from financial systems like ERP, accounts payable and expense tools, plus SSO data and direct integrations. From there, Zylo flags unused licenses, ranks renewals by how much they could save and splits costs across business units. It also tracks AI and usage-based spend as it builds up.


### Where it fits


Zylo fits large enterprises where Procurement or Finance owns software spend, with many business units and hundreds of renewals a year. If you're leaving Zluri because you want deeper spend control at that scale, Zylo is built for it.


### Where it falls short


Zylo is built for spend, not access. Its deprovisioning is about reclaiming unused licenses. Its product pages don't describe access requests, access reviews or creating accounts for new hires, so access management would still need another tool. Pricing is quote-only, and[Vendr's data](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/zylo) puts the median buyer at about $36,000 a year.


### Bottom line


Pick Zylo if you're a large enterprise and spend is the job. It doesn't replace what Zluri's access module did.


## Lumos (best for large enterprises focused on access management)


Lumos combines identity governance with SaaS management, and it's one of the tools Zluri compares itself against most often. It covers access requests, access reviews, HRIS-triggered onboarding, app discovery and spend visibility. It supports Okta, Google Workspace and Microsoft Entra as identity sources, with Okta at the centre of the product.


### Where it fits


Lumos fits large organizations with an identity team, Okta in place and most apps already on enterprise plans. Lumos's own comparison page against Zluri describes it as not meant for teams below 200 employees.


### Where it falls short


Integration depth is the limit buyers describe most. Most of the catalog relies on SCIM, which brings the SSO tax with it. Pricing is sales-gated. Lumos's[AWS Marketplace listing](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prodview-g7fmrspbd3c2i) shows $27,000 for a 12-month core platform contract, and[Vendr's data](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/lumos-app) puts the median buyer at about $36,300 a year.


### Bottom line


Lumos is a capable choice for a large enterprise with Okta in place. If many of your apps sit outside SCIM, check coverage app by app. Our[Lumos alternative guide](https://www.accessowl.com/alternatives/lumos-vs-accessowl) has the full comparison.


## Cledara (a lesser-known pick for finance teams that own software spend)


Cledara is less well known than the other tools on this list, but it's worth a look if spend is what you used Zluri for. It describes itself as "software and AI management for finance teams." It's built around one virtual card per subscription, renewals, approvals and accounting sync with tools like Xero, QuickBooks and NetSuite, and it discovers the apps your company pays for or uses.


### Where it fits


Cledara fits companies where Finance owns software spend and wants to stop surprise renewals and duplicate tools. Pricing is public, in pounds. Plans start at £75 a month for up to 20 apps, and modules like IT Management and Spend Optimisation are £150 a month each.


### Where it falls short


Access isn't the core of the product. Cledara's agent can list and remove access when people leave and set up approved new starters, but it's a paid add-on priced per job. If access requests, access reviews and audit evidence for SOC 2 or ISO 27001 are on your list, check what's covered before you buy. Some teams run both, and AccessOwl connects to Cledara as an app, so spend stays with Finance and access runs on its own.


### Bottom line


Cledara is a good pick if your Zluri use was mainly about spend and Finance runs it. If access is the job, pair it with an access tool or pick one built for access.


## Questions to help you pick a Zluri alternative


-


Is your main problem SaaS spend, or getting people the right access on day one and removing it on their last?


-


Which of your apps will the tool actually provision, and which need an enterprise plan first?


-


After the first year's clean-up, what will you still use the tool for every week?


-


How long until onboarding and offboarding run without your IT team touching them?


-


Have you tested the integrations on your own apps before signing?

Yes, if spend management is your first job. Torii and Zluri both started as SaaS spend management platforms, and both provision through each app's API. If access automation is why you're switching, check how many of your apps Torii can create and remove accounts in.
